1. **macOS only initially.** Apple Silicon, macOS 13+. No Linux or Windows code, CI jobs, runners, shims, packaging or portability work until the owner lifts this.
2. Keep platform code isolated behind `platform/` interfaces (clean seams only; no stubs or ports for other OSes).
3. CI/dev scripts target macOS only. Skip any roadmap item for Linux/Windows (M11, M12) and cross-platform CI matrices.

4. **Full Rust port, owner direction2026-10-14.** Stop the former C implementation queue. Port all first-party application/platform/UI/parser/raster/document/animation/MCP code and in-repo development/test tooling to Rust, then complete the existing product finish line. This supersedes the C17 language/build lock and the former two-implementation-worker ceiling. Use as many useful disjoint Luna codex exec workers as available allowance/resources permit; preserve one writer per module and coordinator-only shared integration. # Agent rules

Read [OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md](OWNER-DIRECTIVES.md) first. It overrides conflicting
roadmap and tooling text. Follow the active `work/WO-*.md`; inspect its allowed
and protected paths before editing. Keep each work order buildable, tested,
verified, and recorded in `STATE.md` and the ledgers.

## Platform and product locks

- Initial support is Apple Silicon macOS 13+. Do not add Linux/Windows code,
  shims, CI jobs, runners, packaging, or portability work.
- Keep platform implementations behind `platform/` interfaces; do not add
  stubs for unsupported operating systems.
- Rust for all first-party code is the active owner-approved migration target.

  parser/rasterizer remain locked. Legacy C17 code is preserved as migration
  reference; do not resume old C implementation orders. See ADR-0022.
- Never read, fetch, or copy GPL SVG-editor source. Do not fetch external SVG

## Repository map

- `app/`: executable composition.
- `src/`: base, platform, XML/SVG, scene, raster, document, UI modules as added.
- `docs/research-r4/`: authoritative operating model and roadmap.

## Commands

The commands below are the preserved legacy C workflow. Rust workspace/build
commands become authoritative only through their implementation orders.

- `./dev build`: configure and build Debug.
- `./dev test-fast`: run local Python tests and validate the ledger.
- `./dev verify`: run the Debug build and fast tests.
- `cmake --preset mac-release && cmake --build --preset mac-release`: Release.
- `python3 scripts/ledger.py validate ledger.jsonl`: validate work history.
- `python3 -m unittest`: run Python harness tests when present.

  their work orders implement them; do not claim missing commands run.

## Engineering and safety

Use the contracts in `docs/CODING_STANDARD.md`: explicit ownership, pointer+length
slices, checked size arithmetic, bounded user input, no VLAs, and no unsafe
string functions. Preserve unknown SVG/XML source. Keep generated files in
ignored repo-local directories. Do not install system packages or touch sibling
directories. Add dependencies only through an ADR and pinned provenance record.

Never weaken frozen acceptance tests or oracles. Run commands named by the
active work order, then report exact evidence. Do not invent test or performance
results. Keep source files focused and under 800 lines; split cohesive modules
before they grow further.

item.text: The cache repair is present: shared entries now own stops, carry a `SourceOwner` witness, and include viewport/instance context; controlled cache validation checks those values. I found the remaining contract gap: `ResolvedPaint` cannot communicate a template’s already-published graph stop range, while `ResolveContext` has no builder, scene, or draft token. The cache’s current `stop_range` indexes its owned template stops and is validated against them, so it cannot also safely represent the scene graph range. I’m recording this exact publication/rollback gap before making any substitute.

I removed the prior crate-local cache so the candidate no longer substitutes for the newly seeded shared cache. The remaining stop-publication gap is concrete: `ResolvedPaint` has only `paint` and owned `stops`; `ResolveContext` cannot publish through a scene/draft; and shared cache validation requires its range to index the cache’s owned stop vector. I’m updating the candidate evidence to distinguish the repaired cache contract from this unresolved graph publication contract.

item.text:
**The full PAINT work order remains blocked.** The R2 seed resolves the cache-key blocker, and I removed the crate-local cache substitute. I verified all five seeded shared-file hashes match the seed.

The remaining blocker is graph-stop publication: `ResolvedPaint` returns owned stops but no template identity or published graph range. `ResolveContext` has no builder, scene, or draft token. `GradientCacheEntry.stop_range` indexes its owned template stops, and cache validation requires it to match `paint.stops`; it cannot also hold the range from `SceneBuilder::append_stops`. Appending each result would duplicate stops across painted instances, while reusing graph ranges without draft-scoped invalidation risks stale ranges after rollback. I recorded the required contract gap in [result.md](/Users/megasoft78/Desktop/Freelance/vexel/.cache/WO-RUST-SVG-PAINT-01/worker/artifacts/WO-RUST-SVG-PAINT-01/result.md) and mapped all 23 symbols and 27 algorithms in the parity map.

Implemented edge-span checks and safe linear/radial sampling, including frozen exact RGB sample assertions. Scoped locked offline check passed; all four focused tests passed; work-order validation passed. The resolver and mixed renderer cases remain incomplete. A shared draft-scoped publication contract is needed before I can continue without inventing stop-sharing or rollback semantics.
